prompt: Match each container to what it does with its children.
hint: Section 02 names two and section 03 the third.

pairs.right: Stacks them, the last written on top

right_distractors: Arranges them in a grid of equal cells

prompt: In `SessionRow`, why did a very long course name wrap instead of pushing the minutes off the screen?
hint: Look for the modifier on the inner `Column`.

choices.text: Because `Text` always wraps at half the screen
choices.why: A `Text` takes the width its content needs, up to what it is given; there is no half-screen rule.

choices.text: Its `Column` has `weight(1f)`
choices.why: Right: the minutes and the box were measured first, and the weighted `Column` got the remainder as a fixed width.

choices.text: `spacedBy(12.dp)` reserves room for the minutes
choices.why: `spacedBy` only puts 12 dp between neighbours; it reserves nothing.

choices.text: `fillMaxWidth` on the row shares the width out evenly
choices.why: It makes the row as wide as the screen; how the width is shared is the weight's job.

prompt: When does Roborazzi actually write the PNG that `captureRoboImage` names?
hint: The lesson ran a task with a particular name.

choices.text: Every time the test runs, with any Gradle task
choices.why: An ordinary `testDebugUnitTest` run left no `shots` directory; record mode has to be turned on.

choices.text: Only on a phone or an emulator
choices.why: The pictures in this lesson were written on the JVM, with no device.

choices.text: In record mode, which `recordRoborazziDebug` turns on
choices.why: Right: lesson 21 covers the other two modes, which compare against a recorded picture.

choices.text: When the build type is release
choices.why: The task in this lesson is the debug one; the build type has nothing to do with recording.

prompt: The tests use the qualifier `xhdpi`. How many physical pixels is one `dp` there?
hint: 360 dp came out as 720 pixels.

prompt: A `Box` holds a picture and then a progress ring, in that order. What is drawn on top?
hint: Order in the code is order of drawing.

choices.text: The progress ring
choices.why: Right: the last child written is drawn last, over the others.

choices.text: The picture, because it is larger
choices.why: Size decides the `Box`'s size, not the drawing order.

choices.text: Whichever has the higher elevation set by default
choices.why: Neither child sets an elevation here; the order of the code decides.

choices.text: Neither: a `Box` places them side by side
choices.why: Side by side is a `Row`; a `Box` stacks.

prompt: The badge uses `offset(x = 4.dp, y = (-8).dp)`. What does that change about the `Box` around it?
hint: Offset moves the drawing, not the measurement.

choices.text: Nothing: its measured size is unchanged
choices.why: Right: `offset` changes where the badge is drawn and leaves every size alone.

choices.text: The `Box` grows by 8 dp at the top to make room
choices.why: If it grew, `offset` would be a layout tool; section 03 says to use it for nudging only.

choices.text: The card moves 8 dp down to stay under the badge
choices.why: The card is a separate child and is placed where the `Box` puts it, unaffected.

choices.text: The badge is clipped to the card's corner
choices.why: The screenshot shows the badge crossing the card's edge, whole.

prompt: You need to hide the badge when no session is done. Which is the Compose way?
hint: The second card in the screenshot is the answer.

choices.text: Set the badge's `visibility` to `GONE`
choices.why: A composable has no `visibility` property; that is the older view system's idea.

choices.text: Give it `alpha(0f)` so it is drawn but transparent
choices.why: It would still be measured and still be read by a screen reader; not calling it removes it.

choices.text: Do not call it: wrap the `Text` in `if (sessionsDone > 0)`
choices.why: Right: a composable that is not called puts nothing on the screen.

choices.text: Move it off the screen with a large `offset`
choices.why: It would still exist, and `offset` is for nudging a few dp.

prompt: To put a child in a `Box`'s top right corner in English and its top left corner in Arabic, use `Alignment.Top___`.
hint: Not `Right`.

prompt: `Modifier.background(amber).padding(16.dp)`: where is the yellow?
hint: Each modifier wraps everything after it.

choices.text: Only behind the letters
choices.why: That is the other order, padding first.

choices.text: Behind the letters and the 16 dp of padding
choices.why: Right: the background wraps the padding, so it covers it.

choices.text: Only in the 16 dp ring around the text
choices.why: A background fills its whole area, text included.

choices.text: Nowhere: padding cancels a background written before it
choices.why: Nothing cancels; the order only changes what wraps what.

prompt: A 24 dp icon needs a tap target of 48 dp. Which chain gives it one?
hint: The target is whatever `clickable` wraps.

choices.text: `Modifier.size(24.dp).padding(12.dp).clickable { … }`
choices.why: `clickable` comes last, so it wraps only what is inside the padding.

choices.text: `Modifier.clickable { … }.padding(12.dp)`, on a 24 dp icon
choices.why: Right: `clickable` wraps the 12 dp on each side as well, 24 + 12 + 12 = 48.

choices.text: `Modifier.padding(12.dp).clickable { … }`, on a 24 dp icon
choices.why: Here the padding is outside `clickable`, and a tap in it does nothing.

choices.text: Any of them, because the order of modifiers only affects drawing
choices.why: The order decides what is drawn and what a tap reaches alike.

prompt: A composable passes its `modifier` parameter to an inner `Text` instead of its outer `Row`. What does a caller who passes `Modifier.padding(8.dp)` see?
hint: Who is outermost?

choices.text: Padding around the whole row, as expected
choices.why: That is what passing it to the outer `Row` would give.

choices.text: A compile error
choices.why: It compiles; the mistake is only in where the padding lands.

choices.text: Space around an inner element instead
choices.why: Right: the caller's modifier landed on an inner child it cannot see.

choices.text: Double the padding, 16 dp
choices.why: Double happens when it is passed to two elements.

prompt: Put one element's part of a layout pass in order.
hint: The parent speaks first and last.
items: the child measures its own children, if it has any
the child chooses a size inside the constraints
the parent places the child at an x and a y

prompt: The log said `Text after fillMaxWidth: given Constraints(minWidth = 720, maxWidth = 720, …)`. What did `fillMaxWidth` do?
hint: Compare with the plain `Text` line above it.

choices.text: It stretched the letters to fill 720 pixels
choices.why: The letters are the same size; only the element's width changed.

choices.text: It made 720 the only width allowed
choices.why: Right: a size modifier works by narrowing the constraints the next element receives.

choices.text: It asked the `Column` for more than the screen
choices.why: The maximum is still 720, the screen's width.

choices.text: It told the parent to measure the child twice
choices.why: Each child is measured once per pass; asking twice is an error.

prompt: In the log, how tall in pixels did the whole `Column` come out?
hint: Its last line; three children of 33 each.

prompt: Why can Compose code nest `Row` inside `Column` inside `Box` ten levels deep without the cost the old view system had?
hint: Count how many times a child is measured.

choices.text: Each child is measured at most once per pass
choices.why: Right: with one measurement each, ten levels cost ten measurements, not two to the tenth.

choices.text: Compose flattens nested containers into one at compile time
choices.why: The nesting is real and printed in the log; it is the measuring that is limited.

choices.text: Layout runs on a background thread
choices.why: Nothing in this lesson moves layout off the main thread; the saving comes from measuring once.

choices.text: Containers deeper than three levels are skipped
choices.why: Nothing is skipped; every element appears in the log.

prompt: In the log, the `Text` beside the weighted one was printed first although it is written second. Why?
hint: A weight is a share of something.

choices.text: A `Row` measures its children from right to left
choices.why: Without weights they are measured in order; the weight changes it.

choices.text: Logging is asynchronous, so lines arrive in any order
choices.why: The order is deterministic, and it is the point of the section.

choices.text: Unweighted children are measured first; weighted ones share what is left
choices.why: Right: the weighted `Text` got 720 minus 86, exactly the remainder.

choices.text: Shorter text is always measured first
choices.why: Length has nothing to do with it; the weight does.

prompt: A `Row` 600 pixels wide holds an unweighted child that takes 120 pixels, then two children with `weight(1f)` and `weight(2f)`. How wide is the `weight(2f)` child?
hint: Two thirds of what is left.

prompt: Match each arrangement to where it puts the spare room, as the screenshot drew it.
hint: Look at the edges.

pairs.right: All of it at the end
Between the children, none at the edges
Equal gaps, the two edges included
8 dp between neighbours, the rest at the end

prompt: A `Row` has `horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.SpaceEvenly`, and one child has `weight(1f)`. What does the arrangement do?
hint: Is there any spare room?

choices.text: It spreads the gaps evenly, and the weight shrinks to fit
choices.why: The weight is measured with the remainder; nothing is reserved for gaps.

choices.text: Nothing visible: the weighted child takes all the spare room
choices.why: Right: with a weight in the row, there is no room left to arrange.

choices.text: It throws, because the two cannot be combined
choices.why: The combination compiles and runs; one of them simply has nothing to do.

choices.text: It centres the weighted child
choices.why: A weighted child fills its share; centring applies to spare room, which is gone.

prompt: In a `Row`, which argument decides where its children sit vertically?
hint: Alignment works across the axis the container stacks on.

choices.text: `verticalAlignment`
choices.why: Right: `SessionRow` uses `Alignment.CenterVertically`.

choices.text: `horizontalArrangement`
choices.why: That works along the row, horizontally.

choices.text: `verticalArrangement`
choices.why: That belongs to a `Column`, along its own axis.

choices.text: `contentAlignment`
choices.why: That belongs to a `Box`.

prompt: `ProportionalRow` measures each child with `minWidth` and `maxWidth` both set to its share. What does that leave the child free to choose?
hint: Read the constraints it builds.

choices.text: Its width, between zero and its share
choices.why: Minimum and maximum are equal, so the width is fixed.

choices.text: Nothing at all
choices.why: The height still has a range, from 0 up to what the layout was given.

choices.text: Its height, up to the layout's maximum
choices.why: Right: and the layout then takes the tallest child's height as its own.

choices.text: Its position in the row
choices.why: Placement is always the parent's decision, never the child's.

prompt: Shares 25, 90 and 45 of 656 pixels, each rounded down: the blocks end short of the right edge. What is the smallest change that removes the gap?
hint: Section 07 names it.

choices.text: Use `Float` widths throughout
choices.why: Constraints and placement are in whole pixels; the rounding happens anyway.

choices.text: Let the last child take `width - x`
choices.why: Right: the last block absorbs the pixels the rounding lost.

choices.text: Wrap the layout in `fillMaxWidth`
choices.why: The layout already takes the full width; the gap is inside it.

choices.text: Replace `placeRelative` with `place`
choices.why: That only affects right-to-left languages.

prompt: Inside `Layout`, a child is placed with `placeable.place___(x, 0)` so that the placement mirrors in a right-to-left language.
hint: Relative to the reading direction.

prompt: A screen shows a title at the top and a button pinned to the bottom, with a list taking the space between them. Which layout does that with this lesson's tools?
hint: Which child should get what is left?

choices.text: A `Column` whose middle child has `weight(1f)`
choices.why: Right: title and button are measured first, and the list gets exactly the remaining height.

choices.text: A `Box` with the three children aligned `TopCenter`, `Center` and `BottomCenter`
choices.why: They would overlap: a long list would run under the title and the button.

choices.text: A `Column` with `Arrangement.SpaceBetween` and no weights
choices.why: A long list would take all the height first, pushing the button off the screen.

choices.text: A `Row` with `fillMaxHeight` on the list
choices.why: A `Row` lays children across, not down.

prompt: Which of these change what a child is measured with, rather than only where it is drawn? Choose all that apply.
hint: `offset` was the one that changed only the drawing.

choices.text: `fillMaxWidth()`
choices.why: Yes: it raised the minimum width to the maximum.

choices.text: `offset(x = 4.dp)`
choices.why: No: it moves the drawing and leaves the measurement alone.

choices.text: `weight(1f)` inside a `Row`
choices.why: Yes: it fixes the child's width at its share of the remainder.

choices.text: `padding(16.dp)`
choices.why: Yes: what comes after it is measured with 16 dp less on each side.
